page: Amazon Web Services m5d.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8175M processor running at 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Local storage is bundled, providing 1800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store capacity.

Benchmark data indicates a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is positioned in the bottom 25% across stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded gzip compression tests. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU benchmarks. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached reads and writes also falls within the middle 50% range.

This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring a balanced ratio of compute to memory alongside high-speed local storage. It is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks, which perform at average benchmark levels. It is less optimal for single-threaded applications or large-scale LLM inference, where prompt processing for 70B models registers in the bottom 25%.
